copy_pick.why: Candidate 2 is the only one that skips the 'Somewhere...' opener and stock 'Meanwhile' pivot from recent cards, and it avoids the rehashed supermarket-freezer gag; its tabloid blurb 'MATH BOTS RATTLE EVERY PADLOCK' and fresh 1Password kicker land the encryption story sharply.

doom.driver: Google releases Cogentic papers on integer factorization, discrete logs and more
doom.summary: Integer factorization and discrete logs are the two quiet pillars holding up basically all of internet encryption, and Google just dropped AI research papers on both while Reddit whispers about factoring in P. Add OpenAI pinning down the matrix-multiplication limit and a Hacker News thread that is just 'holy shit' four times, and the machines are having a better Thanksgiving than your passwords. Speaking of which, 1Password picked this week for a security incident. Impeccable timing.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: AI is now landing hits on factorization, matrix multiplication and the Riemann family of problems faster than anyone can read the PDFs.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Regulators waved through a million orbiting AI data centers while Washington tightened chip curbs and grilled Nvidia's returning CEO.

factors.name: Geopolitics

factors.name: Alignment

factors.name: Wild Card

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. An extreme close-up on a single cracked laptop screen filling the entire frame, seen straight on, with the edges of a rain-streaked café window and a sliver of a wet cobblestone street reflected in the glass border. The screen shows a pale, bureaucratic file-listing web page, rendered as chunky pixel blocks: a bold heading bar, ten rows of tiny blue underlined link blobs each ending in a small "PDF" document icon, and a thin gray disclaimer strip at the bottom. The page is lit by a furnace-orange and blood-red glare that pours up from below the frame, as if the laptop sits on a hearth of embers, so every row of links glows brightly and the white page turns molten orange. A huge jagged crack runs diagonally across the screen, and through it bleeds searing red-orange light. Rising out of the crack is a giant padlock made of pixel iron, its shackle split clean in two, with a glowing composite number breaking into two halves like a cleaved stone block. Around it float small ghostly icons of a two-by-two payoff grid, a black-and-white checker matrix, and a node-and-line graph with one edge missing. All are drawn in hot orange and crimson outlines. Shadows and the screen bezel are bruised violet, never black, and the whole frame is bright and legible at phone size. A tiny pixel cursor arrow hovers over the top link, a malevolent, quietly ordinary doorway to ruin.

minor: The padlock carries a legible "37 42" in the art. The prompt asked for a composite number, but the card adds its own numbers, so this could duplicate or clash with them.
The payoff-grid icon at upper right has tiny "$" and "$$" marks. They read as stand-ins for writing and are acceptable.
The link rows, heading bar and footer strip use pixel squiggles in place of text. This is fine at phone size.
The glass-border reflections of the café window and wet street at the top are murky and hard to read, but they are only background.
The crack and glow overlap the lock and the right-hand icons, so the checker matrix and node graph are somewhat cluttered. Both are still recognizable.

dawn.driver: The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel. Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it’s wired up to nerves in the upper part of his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can use his left limb to handle delicate objects…
dawn.summary: Avi Davidson can feel pressure through his left hand again. His new bionic prosthetic is wired into the nerves of his forearm, so for the first time in years he can pick up delicate objects with it, one of a new generation of hands that can sense. Elsewhere, physicists cooled a single positron to near absolute zero for the most precise matter-antimatter comparison yet, and in Austin a Little Free Bakery is giving away pastries and drawing neighbors together.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Physicists trapped a single positron in a wall-free trap and cooled it to near absolute zero, which sets up the most precise comparison yet between matter and antimatter.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: DoorDash aims to deliver two million meals to food banks for free, and its drivers' routes will help keep pantries stocked through the holidays.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Ultra cyclist Jack Thompson rode almost 10,000 miles through all 48 contiguous US states in just 60 days.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: A trial starting in Peru in 2027 will give Indigenous Amazon communities no-strings cash payments to test whether basic income helps keep the rainforest standing.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: ESA's Euclid telescope, built to map dark matter, found its first new comet, an icy wanderer on an orbit that takes thousands of years to complete.

copy_pick.why: Candidate 2's blurb 'AVI'S LEFT HAND, FEELING AGAIN' best fits today's terse two-beat field-notes form, its summary avoids recent openings and signature phrases, and it stays strictly on good news with the real bionic-hand story as driver.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. SILHOUETTE COMPOSITION in a backyard garden on a clean, clear morning. A vast sky behind the scene glows from honey-amber at the horizon to pale soft green overhead, with the low sun just clearing a far line of rooftops. A wooden pergola draped in grapevines arches across the upper frame. Its leaves are dark green silhouettes edged in gold, and a few grape clusters hang backlit like small amber-green lanterns. In the middle distance, a lone wooden telephone pole stands empty against the glow, a quiet echo of the past. In the foreground, a small round patio table is set with a bowl of grapes and a single cream-colored egg in an egg cup. Avi Davidson, a whole figure seated at the table, is a dark silhouette in profile. His left forearm is extended, and the bionic hand pinches one grape between its fingertips with great care. Fine soft-green luminous filaments run from his upper forearm into the hand, glowing against the dark shape as the feeling of touch. Across the table sits a second, smaller whole silhouette, a loved one with no identifying features, leaning in and smiling toward him. A narrow open back doorway of the home stands behind them, a threshold the device has crossed. Dewy grass catches rim light along the bottom edge. Shadows are lifting, and the palette is warm amber, soft green and deep umber silhouettes. Chunky dithered gradients in the sky, crisp pixel clusters on the leaves.

minor: The man's extended bionic forearm is long and thin compared with his torso, and the glowing green filaments read more as a green sleeve. It is still clearly attached at his elbow and shoulder.
The silhouettes of both figures merge with their chairs and with the table legs, so lower bodies and legs are hard to separate. This is expected in a silhouette composition.
The woman's face and smile are not readable. Her hand-on-chin pose is only a dark blob.
The egg cup and grape bowl on the table are small and dark, so they are hard to make out on a phone.
